info.name: Chat Dashboard - Chat flow and real LOS (Dev)
info.description:
One folder per person. Import with los-dev.postman_environment.json and fill the secret variables in Postman (never commit them).

Customer: sign in by LOS (1a, 1b, 2) or by username and password (0 once, then 2), then 3 refresh, join, send, read.
Staff: 1 login, then read, take the conversation, reply.
Run order: Customer, Staff, Checks, Sign out. The Staff folder uses chatConvId and chatPdfId that the Customer folder saves. The last folders are optional checks against real LOS data.

item.name: Customer
item.description: Needs Customer sign-in first. Requests inherit Bearer {{chatCustomerToken}}.

request.description: Leave chatCustomerUsername empty and this creates a throwaway test customer once (then reuses it); fill it in to use your own. Safe to run again: if the username already exists the answer is 409 and the next step signs in. Password 8 to 128 characters.

exec: pm.test('201 created, or 409 when the account already exists (both are fine)', () => pm.expect([201,409]).to.include(pm.response.code));

item.name: 1. Chat login with username and password

request.description: Needs a Chat account: run '0. Register' once. Saves chatCustomerToken and chatCustomerRefresh.

exec: let body; try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { body = null; }
if (!body || !body.data) pm.test('reason: ' + JSON.stringify(body && (body.error || body.message) || 'no JSON'), () => { throw new Error('see test name'); });

request.description: Send one refresh at a time. A refresh token used twice ends the whole sign-in.

exec: pm.test('200 and a new pair', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.environment.set('chatCustomerRefresh', d.refreshToken);  // the old refresh token is dead now
// a number after the LOS sign-in, null after username/password

item.description: Ends both sign-ins and clears the saved tokens.

item.name: Optional: customer sign-in with LOS
item.description: Replaces Customer step 0 and 1. Needs a real LOS customer (customerUsername, customerPin). Skipped unless the environment variable runLos is 'yes' (needs real LOS credentials).

item.name: 1a. LOS login (LOS checks the password)  [LOS path]

request.description: Real LOS login: LOS takes `username` and `password` (set customerUsername and customerPin; the PIN is the password). LOS allows 5 customer logins per 15 minutes: do not run this in a loop. Saves losCustomerToken.

exec: // LOS does not document its login response, so look for the first JWT stored under a key that contains "access".
const n = find(x); if (n) return n;
pm.test('an access token was found in the response', () => pm.expect(token).to.be.a('string'));

item.name: 1b. Check the LOS token's claims  [LOS path]

request.description: Calls LOS with the customer token and checks the claims the Chat backend requires: iss, aud, type, tokenType, userId, exp.

exec: // Reads the claims only (no signature check; the Chat backend does that). The token itself is never printed.
pm.test('type customer, tokenType access', () => { pm.expect(c.type).to.eql('customer'); pm.expect(c.tokenType).to.eql('access'); });
pm.test('userId is a positive integer', () => pm.expect(Number.isInteger(c.userId) && c.userId > 0).to.be.true);
pm.test('no kid header is fine; exp is in the future', () => pm.expect(c.exp * 1000).to.be.above(Date.now()));

request.description: Swaps the LOS customer token for a Chat session. Saves chatCustomerToken and chatCustomerRefresh.

if (!body || !body.data) pm.test('reason: ' + JSON.stringify(body && (body.error || body.message) || 'no JSON'), () => { throw new Error('see test name'); });

item.name: Optional: staff hand-off from LOS Web
item.description: Needs a real LOS staff account. Steps 2 to 4 pass only once LOS issues the Chat hand-off token. Skipped unless the environment variable runLos is 'yes' (needs real LOS credentials).

request.description: Real LOS staff login (20 per 15 minutes). The pack gives the path but NOT the body: the field names below (username, password) are a guess; if LOS refuses, adjust them. Saves losStaffToken.

exec: // LOS does not document its login response, so look for the first JWT stored under a key that contains "access".
const n = find(x); if (n) return n;
pm.test('an access token was found in the response', () => pm.expect(token).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: 30 per minute. Saves losHandoffToken. The tests show whether LOS has made the changes Chat needs: aud chat, tokenType chat-handoff, a jti, a life of about 2 minutes. Until then the first three FAIL, on purpose.

exec: // Reads the claims only (no signature check; the Chat backend does that). The token itself is never printed.
console.log('aud=' + c.aud, 'tokenType=' + c.tokenType, 'role=' + c.role, 'has jti=' + Boolean(c.jti), 'life=' + (c.exp - c.iat) + 's');
pm.test('aud is chat (pending at LOS)', () => pm.expect(c.aud).to.eql('chat'));
pm.test('has a jti (pending at LOS)', () => pm.expect(c.jti).to.be.a('string'));
pm.test('type staff, has a role and userId', () => { pm.expect(c.type).to.eql('staff'); pm.expect(c.role).to.be.a('string'); pm.expect(c.userId).to.be.a('number'); });
pm.test('lives at most 120 seconds', () => pm.expect(c.exp - c.iat).to.be.at.most(120));

item.name: 3. Chat: sign in with the hand-off token

request.description: Run within 2 minutes of step 2. Succeeds only when LOS issues the Chat-specific token (see step 2); today it answers 401, by design. Needs LOS_STAFF_ROLE_MAP to cover the staff member's LOS role, or it is refused. Saves chatStaffToken.

exec: pm.test('a staff session with a mapped role', () => pm.expect(['AGENT','SUPERVISOR','ADMIN']).to.include(d.user.role));
pm.test('401 until LOS issues a Chat hand-off token (expected today)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

item.name: 4. Chat: the same hand-off token cannot be used twice

request.description: Only meaningful after step 3 succeeded. The same token again must be 401 (single use, by jti).

exec: pm.test('401 (reused or not yet accepted)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

item.name: Optional: LOS loan data (endpoints that exist today)
item.description: Confirmed endpoints, called with the customer's own LOS token. Chat does NOT call these itself yet: its machine-to-machine access is pending at LOS. Use them to compare real responses with the pack's illustrative sample. Skipped unless the environment variable runLos is 'yes' (needs real LOS credentials).

request.description: Check loanDetail.loanPurpose, requestedLoanSize (USD), requestedLoanTerm (days), status, ticketNumber, appliedDate.
Contains personal data (national id, salary): Chat does not store it.

item.name: Optional: see real loan data in Chat (run the LOS customer login and loan data first)
item.description: The customer opens a chat about their real LOS application and sends a message; a Chat staff account then sees the conversation and the real loan data, exactly as the dashboard does. Afterwards open the dashboard as that staff member to see the same thing on screen. Skipped unless the environment variable runLos is 'yes' (needs real LOS credentials).

item.name: D1. LOS: the customer's latest application (saves losApplicationId)

request.description: Real LOS data. Saves the application id: the chat must be opened about THIS application, or the agent panel stays empty.

exec: pm.test('the customer has an application', () => pm.expect(a && a.id).to.be.a('number'));

item.name: D2. Chat: customer signs in again (reads the application)

request.description: Run folder A first so losCustomerToken is fresh (LOS customer tokens last 1 hour). The backend reads the application with this token right after sign-in (LOS_BASE_URL must be set). Wait a second before D5.

item.name: D3. Chat: the customer opens the chat about the real application (saves chatConvId)

request.description: Same call the mobile app makes. applicationId is the real LOS application id from D1.

item.name: D4. Chat: the customer sends a message

request.description: This is what the agent sees arrive in the dashboard inbox.

item.name: D5. Chat: a staff member signs in

request.description: A Chat staff account (username and password, created with `pnpm --filter @chat-dashboard/backend user:create-admin` or by an admin). This is NOT the LOS staff sign-in: that only works once LOS issues the Chat hand-off token (folder B). Saves chatStaffToken.

item.name: D6. Chat: the staff member sees the customer's conversation

request.description: The same conversation appears in the dashboard inbox (it waits in the staff queue). 404 here means the staff role cannot see it.

item.name: D7. Chat: the staff member sees the REAL loan data

request.description: This is what the agent panel shows. Must match what LOS returned in D1. null means the backend has not read the application: check LOS_BASE_URL, that D2 ran after D1 and the customer's applications belong to that customer.

exec: pm.test('200 with real data (not null)', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(a).to.not.eql(null); });
pm.test('same application and status as LOS', () => {
console.log('status=' + a.status, 'purpose=' + a.loanPurpose, 'amount(USD)=' + a.requestedLoanSize, 'tenor(days)=' + a.requestedLoanTerm, 'fetchedAt=' + a.fetchedAt);
